questions.q: Why can't the query SELECT Email, COUNT(Id) FROM Lead GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(Id) > 1 alone tell you which Leads to delete?
options: It returns one summary row per email address, not the individual Lead records or their Ids
HAVING is not valid SOQL
COUNT(Id) always returns zero for duplicates
GROUP BY can only be used on Id fields
questions.explain: Aggregate queries return groups. To decide which record survives, you need the record-level extract with Id, dates, and IsConverted.

questions.q: In the Summit Ridge survivor rule, which Lead in a duplicate group always survives?
options: A converted Lead, because its conversion created or linked Account, Contact, or Opportunity records
The Lead with the shortest email address
The Lead with the lowest Id alphabetically
A random Lead chosen by Data Loader
questions.explain: Converted Leads carry the conversion trail. A group with two or more converted Leads goes to manual review instead.

questions.q: Why do the 4,210 Leads with a blank LeadSource stay blank in the cleaning?
options: There is no evidence for the right value, and inventing one would hide the gap
Salesforce forbids updating blank fields
Data Loader cannot write to LeadSource
Blank values are automatically filled after a load
questions.explain: Cleaning standardizes what you can justify. A guessed value is worse than a visible gap.

questions.q: Only 3,540 Leads need a LeadSource update even though 5,470 have a wrong spelling. Why?
options: 1,930 of the wrong ones are surplus duplicates already being deleted, so updating them is wasted work
The other 1,930 were fixed automatically by Salesforce
Data Loader can update at most 3,540 records
1,930 Leads are converted and cannot be edited
questions.explain: 5,470 minus the 1,930 surplus duplicates being deleted leaves 3,540 survivors that actually need the fix.

questions.q: Why write down the expected results of every change before loading anything?
options: So post-load validation can be checked against a prediction, catching anything unexpected
Because Data Loader requires predictions as input
To reduce the number of API calls
Because SOQL will not run without them
questions.explain: A prediction turns validation into a pass/fail check: the counts land where expected, or you investigate.
